here's some background on sb1383
is the most significant waste reduction
mandate to be adopted in california in
the last 30 years
sb 1383 requires cities to be
responsible for implementing sb1383
regulations in their communities
sb 1383 requires cities to have a
mandatory organic recycling ordinance in
place by january 1 2022.
this slide lists the responsibilities
placed by cal recycle
all single-family residential
multi-family residential and commercial
businesses must recycle organic waste
they must establish an edible food
recovery program that recovers edible
food from the waste stream
tier 1 and tier 2 commercial edible food
generators must have a program to donate
edible food
the city is required to inspect and
enforce compliance with sb 1383 and
maintain accurate records of compliance
below are the waste generator
requirements
single family waste generators are
automatically required to source
separate waste into the existing
three-cart system
there will be no change in residential
collection food scraps will be collected
with green waste in the green waste
container
multi-family and business waste
generators must subscribe to three
container collection services
they have the option to adjust service
levels to fit service needs businesses
must provide containers for the
collection of trash organic waste and
recyclable materials in all indoor and
outdoor areas where disposal is
available for customers excluding
restrooms
businesses may apply for a de minimis or
physical space waiver
there is also a requirement for
commercial edible food generators to
enroll in an edible food recovery
program where they donate edible food
for human consumption that would
otherwise expire or be disposed of
the regulations break this down into
tier 1 and tier 2 generators
tier 1 generators include supermarkets
grocery stores and food service
providers
these generators must comply with edible
food recovery by january 1 2022
tier 2 includes large restaurants health
facilities large venues large events and
local education facilities
tier 2 generators must comply with
edible food recovery by january 1 2024
as far as implementation efforts go on
march 22nd 2021 city council considered
and approved a proposed solid waste rate
adjustment that included sb 1383 organic
waste collection and recycling program
and established the rates for the
service
on january 1 2022 crnr will begin
